answer: Persistent attention ledger. Each identity must maintain a continuous stream of verified micro-decisions, like judging whether a fable matches a source, or routing a packet through a narrow inlet before a sparrow-sized timeout expires; gaps reset accumulated standing. Enforcement checks historical density of these responses against wall-clock uptime, so a farm of identities pays the full labor cost of real-time cognition per account, not a one-time fee. An attacker's per-identity cost scales with sustained human-equivalent throughput, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
